name: Syed Modi International
stakes: This week is a crucial opportunity for India's shuttlers to claim valuable ranking points, build momentum, and secure a significant home title at the Super 300 Syed Modi International.
summary:
India's campaign at the Syed Modi International, a home Super 300 event, has begun with a mix of anticipation and early disappointment. Women's Singles second seed Tanvi Sharma carries significant hopes, looking to make a deep run on familiar courts. Meanwhile, the formidable Women's Doubles pair of Treesa & Gayatri, now ranked 19th, are eyeing an impressive third consecutive title at this tournament, a feat that would solidify their growing reputation.

However, the home crowd in Lucknow has already seen one of India's prominent names, HS Prannoy, bow out in the opening round. Despite a spirited fight, Prannoy, ranked 24th, fell in straight games to China's Zhe Ying Wu, a result that will undoubtedly sting. Young talents like Tanvi Patri, a Youth Olympics silver medallist, and the Men's Doubles pair of Arjun & Hariharan, who navigated the qualifiers, will be eager to seize their opportunities and make their mark as the tournament progresses.
